ideas.title: A hill with my face
ideas.critique: Reshaping the real terrain into a landform from a model's reading of a portrait changes what the ground is, and a face-hill seen from the overview is a strong, showable image. It is still a permanent scenery change with a tool-in-the-loop twist (shared with the earlier depth ideas), and it only lands if the face is recognisable as the model's mistake and the creatures use it (beak ridge, eye hollows).

ideas.title: The island remade from a picture
ideas.critique: This is the same idea the critic scored in round 2, reworded: a model's misperception of a photo becomes terrain, so judge it the same. The dreamlike second copy beside the real corner is a good side-by-side, but the first version was the stronger, more personal landform and this one is its plainer sibling, where lumpy bumps may not read as the cottage.
